source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA5 Data Center in Ashburn, Virginia, publishes 32 MW of IT capacity, operated by NTT.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 3200 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 800 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for NTT Ashburn VA5 Data Center. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Virginia has 26 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 20 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 1338.6 MW. NTT Ashburn VA5 Data Center contributes 32 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
